Architecture Hidden Within Nature

Costa Paradiso

On the northern coast of Sardinia, in the historic region of Gallura, lies Costa Paradiso — one of the most remarkable examples of landscape architecture in the Mediterranean.

Created among monumental formations of pink granite, wild Mediterranean vegetation and crystal-clear waters, Costa Paradiso represents a rare approach to residential architecture: a place where buildings are not imposed upon nature, but carefully integrated into it. Here, the landscape itself became the foundation of the architectural vision.

A Vision of Living in Harmony with Nature

The Origin of Costa Paradiso

Costa Paradiso was developed with the intention of creating a residential environment that preserved the extraordinary character of the Sardinian coastline. Unlike traditional resort development, the concept was based on respect for the natural terrain. The project followed several essential principles:

  • preservation of the existing landscape
  • minimal transformation of the natural environment
  • integration of buildings into granite formations
  • protection of native Mediterranean vegetation
  • creation of private spaces connected with the sea

The result was not a conventional holiday settlement, but a unique architectural landscape where every villa has its own relationship with stone, vegetation and the horizon.

The Kingdom of Pink Granite

The Landscape of Costa Paradiso

The defining feature of Costa Paradiso is its extraordinary granite landscape. The ancient pink granite of Gallura creates a natural architecture of its own — massive rocks, smooth sculptural forms and hidden passages shaped by geological time. These formations change their appearance throughout the day:

  • warm golden tones at sunrise
  • intense pink shades in afternoon light
  • deep copper colours during sunset

The granite is not simply a background for architecture. It is the element that defines the identity of the place.

Villas Integrated into the Landscape

Architecture Between Stone and Sea

The architecture of Costa Paradiso follows the natural forms of the terrain. Buildings are positioned among rocks and vegetation, often appearing as natural extensions of the landscape. The characteristic features include:

  • low horizontal structures
  • terraces following the natural contours of the land
  • local stone materials
  • large openings towards the sea
  • gardens merging with native vegetation

The purpose was not to create monumental buildings, but intimate residences where architecture becomes almost invisible. Each villa is unique because each location offers a different dialogue with nature.

Nature as Part of Architecture

The Mediterranean Garden

The gardens of Costa Paradiso are not traditional ornamental gardens. They are Mediterranean landscapes where cultivated plants coexist with wild vegetation. Typical species include:

  • juniper trees shaped by coastal winds
  • myrtle with its delicate fragrance
  • strawberry trees with seasonal fruits
  • olive trees
  • rosemary, lavender and aromatic herbs
  • native shrubs of the Mediterranean maquis

The garden does not separate the house from nature. It creates a transition between architecture and the surrounding landscape.

Hidden Bays and Crystal Waters

The Sea of Costa Paradiso

The coastline of Costa Paradiso is characterised by dramatic cliffs, small secluded beaches and exceptionally clear waters. The sea changes colour depending on the depth and light — from emerald green in sheltered bays to deep blue beyond the rocks.

The rocky coastline creates a sense of privacy and exclusivity, preserving the feeling of a hidden Mediterranean refuge. The relationship between villa and sea is one of the central elements of life in Costa Paradiso.

A Signature Cove

Spiaggia di Li Cossi

Among the many coves of Costa Paradiso, one has become the emblem of the entire coastline: Spiaggia di Li Cossi. Considered one of the most beautiful and most photographed beaches in northern Sardinia, it lies within a natural amphitheatre of pink granite, its fine golden sand meeting water that shifts from pale turquoise to deep emerald with the depth of the sea floor.

The beach is reached on foot, along a scenic coastal path of around ten to fifteen minutes from the village — a walk in itself considered one of the most rewarding in Gallura, tracing red granite cliffs above the sea before descending toward the cove. A small stream runs down to the shore alongside the trail, and wild Mediterranean flowers cover the rock in spring and early summer.

Sheltered, compact and framed by stone on every side, Li Cossi captures in a single place everything that makes Costa Paradiso singular: granite, sea and untouched nature, standing exactly as they have for millennia.

A Place of Privacy, Beauty and Silence

Life in Costa Paradiso

Costa Paradiso offers a unique Mediterranean lifestyle based on connection with nature. Here, daily life follows the rhythms of the landscape: morning light on granite rocks, evenings overlooking the sea, the scent of Mediterranean plants and the changing colours of the sky.

The value of Costa Paradiso lies not only in its location, but in the atmosphere it creates — a rare combination of privacy, natural beauty and architectural harmony.

A Timeless Mediterranean Heritage

Costa Paradiso Today

Costa Paradiso remains one of the most distinctive residential landscapes in Sardinia. Its uniqueness comes from the balance between human creativity and natural forces. The architecture does not compete with the landscape — it preserves it.

The villas, gardens, granite formations and sea views form a single composition — an example of how contemporary living can exist in harmony with the ancient beauty of nature.

A Place Between Earth and Sea

Costa Paradiso is more than a geographical location. It is a philosophy of living: to wake up surrounded by ancient stone, to look through architecture towards the endless sea, and to experience a landscape where nature remains the greatest work of art.
